article.headline: Moonvalley's Marey Promises the Camera Precision AI Video Has Lacked
article.lede: Paul Trillo, who directed the first music video ever made with OpenAI's Sora, is publicly demonstrating Marey — a video-generation model from Moonvalley that lets a filmmaker specify exact camera moves at exact moments in a generated clip. The feature, keyframe-accurate camera control, addresses the limitation that has kept AI video at arm's length from professional production: until now, the camera did whatever it liked. The demo lands with an unusual legal footnote: Moonvalley trained its model exclusively on licensed footage and indemnifies users against copyright claims, a distinction that matters in a field currently in active litigation.
article.body:
Moonvalley, a Toronto-and-Los-Angeles startup that has raised roughly $154 million from investors including General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, Comcast (CMCSA), and Creative Artists Agency, named its flagship video-generation model *Marey* after Étienne-Jules Marey — the French physiologist whose *chronophotography* predated cinema itself, capturing motion in sequences of still images more than a decade before the Lumière Brothers' first public projection. The gesture is deliberate: **Moonvalley's central claim is that it has rebuilt cinema's foundational problem — the controlled capture of motion — for the generative-AI era.** The company further distinguishes itself by training exclusively on licensed footage, including content acquired through Vimeo (VMEO), and by offering commercial copyright indemnification to users — a contrast to Runway, OpenAI's Sora, and others that face active litigation over their training data.

The feature Trillo demonstrates — *keyframe-accurate camera control* — addresses what has been the central limitation of AI video since the medium emerged. Earlier models accepted a starting frame and a text prompt, then generated all subsequent frames probabilistically: the camera might pan left or right, a character's hand might drift, a background element might dissolve without warning. Directors had no reliable control over what would happen at second three of a five-second clip. Marey's system changes that contract. Users place reference images or video frames at specific points on a timeline; the model must honor every anchor and construct a physically coherent path between them. A cursor-based interface then lets a director draw the precise camera trajectory — *dolly* speed, pan arc, zoom rate — through a three-dimensional space the model infers from the input image. The result is a shot that is repeatable and specifiable: the two things a working production most needs.

The significance is less technical than structural. Frame-precise control is what moves AI video from a demonstration medium to a production tool. Director Ángel Manuel Soto credited Marey with cutting his production costs by 20 to 40 percent — a credible figure when you consider what it replaces: location scouts, camera operators, and full crew rates for *pre-visualization* shots that no audience ever sees. Edward Ulbrich, the visual-effects pioneer behind *Titanic* and *The Curious Case of Benjamin Button*, joined Moonvalley partly on the strength of that precision argument. Adobe (ADBE) integrated Marey into its Firefly Boards platform in late 2025, placing it alongside Runway as one of two dominant generation engines available to enterprise creative teams.

The choice of messenger matters. Trillo is not an AI evangelist — he is a working director who built a 50-Nokia-phone bullet-time rig and directed a drone-only single-take film long before generative AI existed. In 2024 he directed the music video for Washed Out's "The Hardest Part," the first officially commissioned video made with OpenAI's unreleased Sora model, generating roughly 700 clips over six weeks and editing 55 into a continuous-zoom illusion tracking a couple across decades. He has since become a formal partner in Asteria, Moonvalley's in-house production studio. His public endorsement of Marey's camera-control system carries a weight that conventional influencer promotion would not.

The broader market is fragmenting fast. Runway is pivoting toward editorial manipulation of existing footage rather than generation from scratch. Kling, the model from Kuaishou (1024.HK), has found a market in performance-marketing automation at scale. Sora, despite its brand recognition, remains slow and expensive for professional use. Moonvalley is betting that the segment willing to pay for precision — narrative filmmakers, brand studios, streaming platforms — is large enough to sustain a distinct company, particularly one that can offer what the others cannot: a clear legal *chain of title* over its training data.

concepts.definition: A 19th-century photographic technique that captured successive phases of motion in a sequence of images taken at rapid, regular intervals. Étienne-Jules Marey perfected the method with his 'chronophotographic gun' in 1882, enabling scientists and artists to study movement — of birds, horses, and humans — in ways the naked eye could not perceive. It is a direct ancestor of cinema, and the namesake of Moonvalley's model.

In traditional animation, a keyframe marks a moment in time where a visual property — position, lighting, camera angle — is explicitly defined; software interpolates everything in between. In AI video generation, 'keyframe accuracy' means the model is constrained to produce specific, user-specified frames at particular timestamps, rather than generating all motion probabilistically from a single starting image. This transforms the model from a creative suggester into a precision executor.

A camera movement in which the camera itself physically moves forward or backward along a track, creating a sense of depth and immersion distinct from a zoom, which changes only the focal length. In AI video, simulating a dolly move requires the model to infer a three-dimensional scene from a two-dimensional image and render the parallax and perspective shifts that real camera motion would produce.

A production technique in which rough approximations of planned shots — animations, storyboards, or video sketches — are created before principal photography begins. Previz lets directors, cinematographers, and editors work through shot design, timing, and blocking without the cost of a full crew. AI video generation can now serve as a high-fidelity previz tool, replacing work traditionally done by specialized studios.

A legal term for the documented sequence of copyright ownership, licensing agreements, and permissions that establishes who holds the rights to a piece of creative work. In AI, a 'clean' chain of title over training data means every piece of content used to train a model was licensed with permission — critical for commercial users who need legal protection against copyright infringement claims.

A legal guarantee offered by a vendor to its customers that the vendor will cover legal costs and damages if the customer's use of the vendor's product results in a copyright infringement claim. In AI video, this matters because models trained on unlicensed content expose users to liability; indemnification shifts that risk back to the AI company, making the product viable for large commercial productions.

ticker_cmcsa.name: Comcast Corporation
ticker_cmcsa.blurb: Comcast Corporation is a global media and technology company operating through five segments: Residential Connectivity & Platforms, Business Services Connectivity, Media, Studios, and Theme Parks. It provides broadband, wireless, and video services to residential and business customers, along with content production and theme park operations. With a market cap of about $94.45 billion and revenue of $125.28 billion (TTM), Comcast is a leading player in the telecommunications and media industry.
ticker_cmcsa.recent: As of May 6, 2026, CMCSA stock closed at $26.44, near its 52-week low of $25.75, reflecting a 27% decline from its high. The company reported earnings on April 23, 2026, with net income up 19.7% year-over-year. Analysts have a buy rating with a price target of $34.54, suggesting potential upside of over 30%.

ticker_vmeo.name: Vimeo.com, Inc.
ticker_vmeo.blurb: Vimeo.com, Inc. provides video software solutions, including hosting, editing, live-streaming, and AI-powered tools for businesses and creative professionals. The company serves a range of customers from small businesses to large enterprises, with a focus on high-quality, ad-free video experiences. As of November 2025, Vimeo was acquired by Bending Spoons US and delisted from NASDAQ.
ticker_vmeo.recent: On November 24, 2025, Vimeo was delisted from NASDAQ after being acquired by Bending Spoons US for $1.38 billion in cash, with shareholders receiving $7.85 per share. The acquisition closed in late November 2025, ending Vimeo's public trading history.

ticker_adbe.name: Adobe Inc.
ticker_adbe.blurb: Adobe Inc. is a multinational software company known for its creative, marketing, and document management solutions, including Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat Reader, and the Experience Cloud. The company has transitioned to a subscription-based model, generating recurring revenue from its Digital Media and Digital Experience segments. Adobe holds a dominant position in the creative software market and competes with firms like Salesforce and Microsoft in the digital experience space.
ticker_adbe.recent: In the past 30 days, Adobe's stock has shown volatility amid broader tech market movements. The company reported strong quarterly earnings, beating analyst estimates on both revenue and earnings per share, driven by growth in its Digital Media segment. However, forward guidance was slightly below expectations, leading to mixed analyst reactions.

ticker_1024-hk.name: Kuaishou Technology
ticker_1024-hk.blurb: Kuaishou Technology operates a leading short-video and live-streaming platform in China, known for its community-driven content and e-commerce integration. The company generates revenue through live-streaming gifts, advertising, and online shopping commissions. It competes with ByteDance's Douyin in the Chinese social media market.
ticker_1024-hk.recent: In the past 30 days, Kuaishou's stock has shown volatility with price swings of up to 7% in a single day. Analysts from Citi and UBS raised price targets to HKD95 and HKD108 respectively, reflecting optimism about the company's growth prospects. Block trades totaling millions of shares have been reported, indicating institutional activity.

poster_paultrillo.blurb: LA-based writer, director, artist, and partner at Asteria Films. Known for experimenting with AI tools like OpenAI's DALL-E 2 and RunwayML to create surreal, fluid visual art, often blending architecture and animation. His work explores the intersection of AI and filmmaking, with viral threads demonstrating techniques like outpainting and frame interpolation.
